name: 4 machine learning categories
detail: Label availability and intended purpose determine suitability.
source: Study Guide D2: Machine learning algorithms

name: 4 confusion-matrix outcomes
detail: TP caught fraud; FP legitimate flagged; FN fraud missed; TN legitimate correctly cleared.
source: Study Guide D2: Fraud detection model evaluation

name: Precision = TP/(TP+FP)
detail: Of all flagged fraud, share truly fraudulent; low precision implies avoidable customer friction.
source: Study Guide D2: Model evaluation metrics

name: Recall = TP/(TP+FN)
detail: Of all genuine fraud, share detected; low recall implies missed loss exposure.
source: Study Guide D2: Model evaluation metrics

name: F1 = 2×precision×recall/(precision+recall)
short: Harmonic mean of precision and recall
detail: Balances the two positive-class measures.
source: Study Guide D2: Model evaluation metrics

name: Specificity = TN/(TN+FP)
detail: Share of genuine non-fraud correctly cleared.
source: Study Guide D2: Model selection metrics

name: Accuracy = (TP+TN)/Total
detail: Can be misleading when non-fraud transactions overwhelmingly outnumber fraud.
source: Study Guide D2: Fraud detection model metrics

name: Worked example: 1,000 transactions
detail: Precision 50%; recall 75%; F1 60%; accuracy 98%. High accuracy does not imply good fraud capture.
source: Memorisation Guide M2: Model evaluation example

name: 3 fraud detection layers
short: Customer baseline · Organization baseline · Known fraud
